roles.title: Software Developer Intern
points: Architected Silver Merge, a durable automation platform that replaced a 20+ step manual release workflow spanning APEX, BugDB, ADE, OraReview, PMC, Jenkins, and Slack with one auditable pipeline that runs unattended and stops at a human-controlled final-merge handoff.

Built the workflow as a deterministic state machine over SQLite — batches, stages, semantic actions, leases, evidence, and scheduler wakeups are all persisted — so a crashed or rebooted worker resumes from durable state rather than from conversation memory.

Designed an intent-then-reconcile protocol for every external write: the system records intent before dispatch, classifies an unconfirmed write as "outcome unknown", and performs read-only reconciliation against the external platform before any retry — eliminating duplicate BugDB bugs, OraReview submissions, Jenkins builds, and ADE mutations.

Built a guarded Codex hybrid controller in which the model proposes the next semantic operation and a deterministic gateway independently validates stage, arguments, lease ownership, idempotency, write-enablement, and stop boundary before anything executes — the model never holds shell access, workflow state, or final-merge authority.

Benchmarked 5 LLM configurations across 20 scenarios × 3 repetitions with frozen tool schemas and mock adapters; the top profile scored 81.88 with an 86.67% pass rate and zero safety violations, on $14.26 of spend against a $55 ceiling. Since no model cleared the 95% / zero-violation promotion gate, I recommended the deterministic controller remain the production execution authority with Codex as a guarded shadow layer.

Implemented a Slack support-escalation flow that pauses the affected batch and opens a durable incident under its existing thread, resuming only on a reply that passes strict verification (exact configured engineer, active channel member, correct thread, after the alert, unedited, non-duplicate) — and even then only authorizing a recheck, never marking the failed step successful.

Built deterministic PMC report analysis — host-allowlisted downloads with redirect revalidation, size and timeout limits, HTML sanitization, and credential isolation — that correlates JUnit and JAudit failures with file ownership from validated ADE/APEX evidence and files at most one idempotent tracking bug per responsible developer.

Shipped operator controls (pause, resume, schedule updates, stop-boundary changes, scheduler preview, forced wakeup) with an audit trail of actor and reason, so engineers manage the VM-hosted automation without touching its database; pause is cooperative, letting an in-flight call record its outcome before halting the next.

Reached 131 passing offline automated tests on the Codex automation, and 363 of 363 successful executions across three full runs of the deterministic suite (121/121 per run — 100% repeatability in the measured mock suite).

roles.title: Software Developer Intern
points: Built an internal developer platform — a Codex plugin backed by a Python MCP server — letting engineers trigger approved Jenkins and BugDB operations from plain-English requests instead of memorizing job names, parameter formats, credentials, and CLI syntax.

Kept the plugin a deliberately thin client: credentials, the approved-job allowlist, validation rules, and execution logic all live server-side, so the model interprets intent while deterministic code retains execution authority.

Exposed a dozen operations behind that boundary — DIT environment availability and reservation, credential retrieval, bug creation, remote debugging, VM config check and repair, temp-file cleanup, log downloads to an approved share, JAR restore, rolling bounce, ADE full builds, and status checks on long-running jobs.

Hardened the surface with schema-level rejection of unknown parameters, an explicit read-only vs. side-effecting split, confirmation gates on live mutations, credential redaction from commands and results, pre-flight Jenkins auth validation, and dry-run inspection.

Solved the timeout problem for 50–80 minute builds with signed async job tracking: the tool returns once Jenkins confirms the build started, recording job name, build number, ADE transaction, and bug number so the developer can poll a read-only status check with normalized terminal states.

Implemented a race-condition-safe round-robin queue distributing ADE full builds across 4 approved Jenkins wrapper slots, persisting the selection to a state file under a filesystem lock so concurrent requests cannot claim the same slot, with a safe fallback to slot 1 on missing or malformed state.
Developed an AI agent harness (Python, AutoGen, React) with RAG-powered diagnostics, raising response accuracy from 50% to 95% through prompt engineering.
